title: Simone Ashley Revived a 21-Year-Old Alexander McQueen Gown at Cannes — and the Diaspora Is Claiming Her
excerpt: The British-Tamil 'Bridgerton' star wore a crimson masterpiece first seen on Gisele Bündchen, cementing her place as South Asian fashion royalty on the Riviera.
body:
The 79th Cannes Film Festival has had no shortage of showstoppers, but when Simone Ashley stepped onto the red carpet for the premiere of Karma, she wasn't just wearing a dress — she was wearing history.

The British-Tamil actress chose a vintage Alexander McQueen gown from the designer's Fall 2005 collection: a deep crimson, structured mermaid silhouette with a sculpted bodice and dramatic pleated skirt. The same dress was previously worn by Gisele Bündchen and Cate Blanchett, making Ashley the third woman — and the first South Asian — to carry the piece on a global stage.

A Stylist's Masterstroke

The look was assembled by Rebecca Corbin-Murray, the London-based stylist who has quietly become one of the most influential voices in celebrity dressing. Corbin-Murray paired the gown with dazzling diamond jewelry from Chaumet, the French maison, keeping accessories minimal so the dress could do the heavy lifting.

"There's something about vintage couture that says you don't need the newest thing to be the most interesting person in the room," a fashion critic noted on social media. "Simone understood the assignment."

The result was a red-carpet moment that blended old-Hollywood grandeur with the kind of confidence that only comes from knowing exactly who you are.

Why NRIs Are Paying Attention

Simone Ashley — born Simone Ashwini Pillai in Camberley, Surrey, to Tamil parents — has become one of the most visible South Asian faces in global entertainment. Her breakout as Kate Sharma in Bridgerton Season 2 made her a household name, and since then, she's been building a fashion identity that feels distinctly her own: bold, structured, unapologetically glamorous.

For the Indian diaspora, particularly in the UK and North America, Ashley represents something specific. She's not a Bollywood export or a heritage casting choice. She's a British-born Tamil woman who earned her way into one of the most-watched Netflix franchises in history — and now she's commanding Cannes.

The McQueen Connection

Alexander McQueen's 2005 collection was one of his most theatrical — runway pieces that were closer to sculpture than clothing. The crimson gown Ashley wore was designed during a period when McQueen was at the height of his creative powers, producing work that remains among the most coveted vintage fashion in the world.

That a South Asian actress is now part of that gown's lineage is not lost on fashion watchers. The piece has traveled from a Brazilian supermodel to an Australian-born Oscar winner to a Tamil-British Netflix star — a journey that mirrors fashion's own slow reckoning with who gets to wear the most important clothes.

What Comes Next

Ashley's Cannes appearance is part of a broader push. She's expected at multiple events during the festival's run through May 23, and her upcoming film slate — still under wraps — suggests she's moving beyond the Bridgerton universe. For NRI audiences who've followed her trajectory from a supporting role in Sex Education to global red-carpet royalty, the McQueen moment at Cannes feels less like a fashion choice and more like a coronation.

Cannes 2026 runs through May 23. Simone Ashley's film Karma premiered on the festival's opening weekend.
